text:
maria_support: hey team, customer reported 401s on their Dedicated ingress only when traffic goes through our LB + Istio path. Directly hitting the pod IP succeeds. they say SSO login + portal works, but API calls from their backend -> our endpoint fail with 401. sharing repro and a few logs i captured.

maria_support: repro steps i used:
1) curl directly to pod (pod ip:8443) - works
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer ey...abc' https://10.3.45.12:8443/v1/predict
> HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
2) curl to customer-dedicated.example.com (LB + istio) - 401
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer ey...abc' https://customer-dedicated.example.com/v1/predict
> HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid_token"}
```
3) checked LB access log - shows Authorization header present in client request (we log raw headers)
```
[LB] 10.9.8.7 - - "GET /v1/predict HTTP/1.1" 401 - Header: Authorization: Bearer ey...abc
```
4) but app logs (on pod) show no Authorization header received. app prints headers on debug route: header Authorization: <missing>

maria_support: i also tried adding X-Forwarded-Authorization: Bearer ey...abc and that still returns 401 (app doesn't check that header). looks like header is being removed or rewritten between LB and app. customer is blocked. filing here for triage, repro steps attached.

alex_enginfra: thanks maria. first suspicion: our ingress gateway (envoy/istio) strip or normalizes the Authorization header depending on ext_authz or header policy. can you paste the envoy access logs from the ingress-gateway pod for the same request? also which mesh version?

maria_support: mesh v1.15.2. envoy access log from ingress-gateway:
```
[ingress-gw] "GET /v1/predict HTTP/1.1" 401 - upstream_service: customer-backend; request_headers: {
  ":method": "GET",
  ":path": "/v1/predict",
  ":authority": "customer-dedicated.example.com",
  "authorization": "Bearer ey...abc",
  "x-forwarded-for": "10.9.8.7"
}
```
alex_enginfra: so ingress sees it. can you capture from the istio-proxy sidecar on the app pod? run `kubectl exec -it <app-pod> -c istio-proxy -- bash` and tail the envoy logs or run `tcpdump -n -i any port 8443` to see raw packets. if header disappears inside mesh, it's likely ext_authz or an HTTP header whitelist.

jamie_oncall: i grabbed the sidecar logs while hitting the LB. envoy shows the request arriving and shows the header in the first recv, but the request forwarded to the app lacks it. snippet:
```
[sidecar] recv headers: authorization: Bearer ey...abc
[sidecar] forwarded headers: (authorization absent)
```
jamie_oncall: reproduced locally with customer token. so this is not a one-off.

ravi_engplatform: two places to check: 1) istio ext_authz filter (if enabled, it may request authz service and then not reattach header), 2) if we have an ingress nginx in front doing `proxy_set_header` incorrectly. what does `kubectl get envoyfilter -n customer-namespace` show?

maria_support: output:
```
NAME              AGE
ext-authz-filter   3d
```

ravi_engplatform: bingo. open the ext_authz config. many of our ext_authz adapters explicitly remove sensitive headers when doing a check then expect the authz service to re-inject them. if the adapter is misconfigured, it won't put them back. paste ext_authz config pls.

maria_support: config snippet:
```
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: ext-authz-filter
spec:
  configPatches:
  - applyTo: HTTP_FILTER
    match:
      context: GATEWAY
    patch:
      operation: INSERT_BEFORE
      value:
        name: envoy.filters.http.ext_authz
        typed_config:
          '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.ext_authz.v3.ExtAuthz
          http_service:
            server_uri:
              uri: http://authz.customer.svc.cluster.local:8080/check
            authorization_request:
              allowed_headers:
                patterns:
                  - exact: ":method"
                  - exact: ":path"
                  - exact: ":authority"
                  - exact: "x-forwarded-for"
              # Authorization not listed here
```

lee_security: aha. allowed_headers list does NOT include `authorization`, so envoy strips it before calling authz (and since the filter isn't configured to pass-through/reinstate it, it never gets forwarded to upstream). this is intentional for some setups but breaks our token-introspection flow where the upstream needs the bearer token post-authz. we should either add `authorization` to allowed_headers or configure `include_request_headers_in_check` differently.

ravi_engplatform: note: adding `authorization` to allowed_headers means the token will be forwarded to the authz service (ok) AND envoy will reattach it if configured. we have to be careful about exposing tokens to the authz service logs. need a threat assessment.

lee_security: quick mitigation: configure ext_authz to explicitly add `authorization` back to the request headers on successful check. snippet suggestion:
```
authorization_response:
  allowed_upstream_headers:
    patterns:
      - exact: "authorization"
```

alex_enginfra: i'll prepare a patch for the EnvoyFilter in customer namespace to include authorization in both allowed request headers and allowed_upstream_headers. plan: deploy to staging first and run regression. @ops-bot can you run canary deploy for the filter? :pray:

ops-bot: canary deployment started for EnvoyFilter ext-authz-filter in namespace customer-namespace. rollout id: rf-2026-11. ETA ~5m.

jamie_oncall: after applying temp patch to staging, i re-ran curl -> now the app receives Authorization header and returns 200. test tokens with introspection also succeed. hashing this as the root cause: ext_authz filter had a restrictive allowed_headers list.

customer_jess: thanks team! the customer's backend is unblocked. they want to know whether this change will be applied to prod and whether there are security implications.

lee_security: security notes: forwarding auth header to authz is fine if authz is internal and mTLS enforced. we should enable `allowed_upstream_headers` only for namespaces with mTLS and set RBAC to prevent log exfiltration. i'll draft a short runbook.

ravi_engplatform: next steps:
- alex will PR change to add `authorization` to allowed_headers + allowed_upstream_headers on the EnvoyFilter (staging + canary) (ETA 2h)
- security to review runbook (ETA 6h)
- support to notify customer of prod timeline (maria)
- add an automated smoke test that hits dedicated endpoints and verifies Authorization passthrough (ravi)

maria_support: i'll update the customer and keep thread posted. nice triage everyone. :tada:

alex_enginfra: opening PR now: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/patches/2345 - includes test plan and risk assessment.

ops-bot: canary finished: 100% success in staging clusters. no sidecars restarted during change.

jamie_oncall: i'll monitor dedicated ingress for 30m after prod rollout. set alert if 5xx or 401 spike > 5% from baseline.

maria_support: closing loop with customer, they asked for a postmortem/summary once prod is complete. i'll collect notes here for that doc.
